angularDiameterSource: Uniform-disc fit to the 780 averaged squared visibilities of the pinned February 2020 VLT/MATISSE continuum data (3.94-4.00 um), this package; Drevon et al. (2024, MNRAS Letters 527, L88) report 43.8 mas for the same epoch and 42.5 mas for December 2018.
radiusSource: Joyce et al. (2020): 764 (+116/-62) solar radii at 695700 km. The pinned angular diameter at the adopted distance gives 767 solar radii, 0.4 percent larger.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 3600 ± 25 K from Levesque & Massey 2020 (ApJL 891, L37; https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10463), abstract and Section 3: MARCS model fits to optical spectrophotometry of 15 February 2020, during the Great Dimming. The radius source, Joyce et al. 2020, adopts this value in its Table 2.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius. The photosphere of a red supergiant is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp; the sphere is the reference surface the interferometric image is cast onto, not a measured shape.
